alt: Monte Albán main plaza with Building J and the North Platform, Oaxaca
caption: The levelled main plaza of Monte Albán, with the angled Building J and the North Platform. This is the Day 3 opening-time visit, before tour buses arrive, to one of Mesoamerica's earliest cities.

alt: Baroque facade of the Church of Santo Domingo de Guzmán in Oaxaca city
caption: The carved stone facade of Santo Domingo de Guzmán, the Dominican church in Oaxaca's historic centre. It anchors the Day 2 walk through the colonial city between market stops.

attribution: Amante Darmanin from Malta — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Pine-covered highland ridges near San Antonio Cuajimoloyas in the Sierra Norte
caption: Cool highland terrain near Cuajimoloyas, the Pueblos Mancomunados trailhead at about 3,000 m. Day 5 starts here, and the near-freezing nights explain the layers advised for the village-to-village trek.

commonsFile: File:Ábside del templo conventual de Yanhuitlán, Oaxaca.JPG
attribution: Suitersibor — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Rear apse of the Dominican convent church of Santo Domingo Yanhuitlán
caption: The massive stone apse of the 16th-century Dominican convent at Yanhuitlán. It is a headline stop of the Day 9 loop through the Mixteca Alta.

commonsFile: File:Mole negro de Oaxaca con arroz.jpg
attribution: ProtoplasmaKid — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Plate of mole negro with rice and chicken in Oaxaca
caption: Mole negro, the dark, many-ingredient sauce at the centre of Oaxacan cooking. It is what the Day 2 market-and-cooking-class experience is built around.

attribution: Eve Flor — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Stall at a Oaxaca market selling heaped mole pastes in several colours
caption: A market vendor's piled mole pastes, one for each of Oaxaca's classic moles. Choosing ingredients at a central market is the first half of the Day 2 mole class.

commonsFile: File:Galería de los Danzantes en Monte Albán, Oaxaca.jpg
attribution: Mario Yaír TS — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The Danzantes gallery at Monte Albán with carved stone relief slabs
caption: The Danzantes gallery at Monte Albán, whose carved slabs are among the oldest writing-era monuments in Mesoamerica. It is the close-up stop of the Day 3 site visit.

commonsFile: File:Exconvento de Santiago apóstol de Cuilápam 02.jpg
alt: The former Santiago Apóstol convent at Cuilápam de Guerrero
caption: The unfinished 16th-century Dominican convent of Santiago Apóstol at Cuilápam, in the valley south-west of the city. It is one of the options for the flexible Day 10 around Cuilapan and Zaachila.

attribution: El Ágora — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Panorama of the archaeological site of Zaachila in the Oaxaca valley
caption: Zaachila, the late Zapotec and Mixtec capital, seen across its excavated mounds. It pairs with Cuilápam on the flexible Day 10 in the valley.

commonsFile: File:San Pedro y San Pablo Teposcolula.jpg
attribution: WeltKonnte — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The plaza and Dominican church of San Pedro y San Pablo Teposcolula
caption: The plaza of Teposcolula with its Dominican church, in a high Mixtec town. It is the second Mixteca Alta stop on Day 9, after Yanhuitlán.

attribution: Vlahebo — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Santa Catarina Lachatao, Sierra Norte, Oaxaca
alt: The dome and towers of the village church of Lachatao in the Sierra Norte
caption: The village church of Lachatao, the old mining settlement in the Sierra Norte. It is where the Day 7 walk from Latuvi ends.

attribution: Davidanegas — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Painted wooden alebrije animals displayed for sale in San Martín Tilcajete
caption: Hand-carved and painted alebrije figures in San Martín Tilcajete. The village is one of the craft stops on Day 4 in the southern valleys.
